rejected.title: Plant transport and support
card: Roots
take up water and minerals from the soil. They also anchor the plant in the ground.
Xylem
tubes that carry water, and the minerals dissolved in it, up from the roots to the stem and leaves.
Phloem
tubes that carry sugars made in the leaves to other parts of the plant, such as roots and fruits.
Stems
hold the leaves up towards the light. The xylem and phloem run through the stem, linking the roots and the leaves.
rejected.remember: Xylem moves water up from the roots. Phloem moves sugars from the leaves. Stems hold the plant up.

a.q: Which part of a plant carries sugars made in the leaves to the rest of the plant?
opts: Phloem
Xylem
Roots
Stem
a.why: Phloem tubes carry sugars from the leaves to other parts of the plant. Xylem is the most tempting wrong answer, but it carries water and minerals up from the roots.
a.clue: Which tubes move sugars rather than water?

b.q: Priya cuts the bark and phloem in a ring around a tree branch. The xylem inside is left unharmed. What is most likely to happen to the leaves beyond the cut?
opts: They still get water, but sugars cannot leave them
They get no water, but sugars can still leave them
They get no water and sugars cannot leave them
They still get water and sugars still leave them
b.why: The xylem is unharmed, so water and minerals can still travel up to the leaves. The phloem is cut, so sugars made in those leaves cannot be carried away to other parts of the plant.
b.clue: Which tubes were cut, and what do they carry?

version.title: Plant transport and support
card: Roots
take in water and dissolved minerals from the soil, mostly through tiny root hairs. They also anchor the plant in the ground.
Xylem
tubes that carry water and minerals up from the roots, through the stem, to the leaves.
Phloem
tubes that carry sugars made in the leaves to the parts that use or store them, such as growing tips, roots and fruit.
Stems
hold the leaves up towards the light. The xylem and phloem run through the stem, linking the roots and the leaves.
version.remember: Water goes up in the xylem, sugars move out of the leaves in the phloem, and the stem holds it all up.

a.q: A carrot stores sugar in its root, but the sugar is made in its leaves. How does the sugar reach the root?
opts: Through the phloem
Through the xylem
Through the root hairs
Through water in the soil
a.why: Sugars made in the leaves travel in the phloem to the parts that store them, such as the carrot's root. Xylem carries water up from the roots, the other way.

b.q: Celery stalks are stood in water mixed with blue food dye. A day later, thin blue lines run up the stalks to the leaves. Which tubes carried the dye?
opts: The xylem, which carries water up
The phloem, which carries sugars up
The phloem, which carries water up
The root hairs, which carry dye up
b.why: The dye travels with the water, and water moves up the stalk in the xylem. Phloem carries sugars made in the leaves, not water taken in from below.
b.clue: What does the dye travel with?
